title: Cross-Layer Feature Tracking: Do SAE Features Persist or Transform Across Layers?
original_idea: Train SAEs on every other layer of GPT-2 Small (layers 0,2,4,6,8,10). Use activation patching to identify cross-layer causal feature correspondences. Build bipartite feature-correspondence graphs.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Cross-layer feature tracking is a prerequisite for attribution graphs. Important technical infrastructure question for safety interpretability.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Training 6 SAEs plus doing activation patching across all of them for 100 features per layer is computationally heavy and methodologically complex for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Six layers of SAEs, 100 features each, pairwise patching across adjacent layers. The combinatorial explosion makes this broader than presented.

title: Minimal Circuit Identification for a Safety-Relevant Binary Decision
original_idea: On GPT-2 Small, find the minimal circuit for gendered vs. gender-neutral pronoun completion via iterative ablation. Test generalization on 50 novel prompts.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Proof-of-concept for interpretability-based behavioral certification. Generalization test adds value beyond existing circuit work.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Well-trodden territory with TransformerLens. Iterative ablation is documented in tutorials. Gender circuit is studied. Feasible in 30hrs.

narrow_scope.reasoning: One binary task, iterative ablation, 90% accuracy threshold, 50 novel test prompts. Clear deliverable. Slightly open-ended in ablation strategy.

title: Testing Whether Linear Probes Deceive: Can a Model Satisfy a Probe While Behaving Inconsistently?
original_idea: Train a linear probe for factual vs. non-factual on GPT-2 Small layer 6. Patch in activation directions corresponding to 'factual' on non-factual prompts. Measure whether behavioral outputs change as predicted.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Directly tests causal validity of probes for safety claims. If probes are not causally meaningful, probe-based safety claims are unfounded. Critical finding.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Linear probes in sklearn plus TransformerLens activation patching. Both well-documented. Feasible for beginners on GPT-2 Small in 30hrs.

narrow_scope.reasoning: One concept, one layer, one model, 100 examples, one intervention type. Extremely focused deliverable.

title: Do Vision Transformer SAE Features Correspond to Human-Recognizable Safety-Relevant Visual Concepts?
original_idea: Train SAE on CLIP-ViT-B/32 via ViT-Prisma on ImageNet + safety-relevant images. Identify top 20 safety-relevant features and have 3 raters score interpretability and safety-relevance (1-5).

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Relevant for multimodal safety but initial/exploratory. Whether 20 features in a small model are interpretable has limited generalization to deployed content moderation.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires ViT-Prisma setup, curating safety-relevant image datasets, SAE training on vision model, recruiting 3 human raters. High coordination overhead for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Dataset curation, SAE training, human rating coordination, statistical analysis. Multiple bottlenecks and dependencies.

title: Assessing Interpretability Completeness: What Fraction of Behavioral Variance Do Identified Circuits Explain?
original_idea: On GPT-2 Small, run full model and IOI circuit-only model on 200 novel IOI prompts. Compute KL divergence between output distributions. Examine whether residual divergence correlates with input features.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Quantifying the completeness gap of the best-documented circuit is valuable meta-interpretability. Directly informs whether circuits are certifiable.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: IOI circuit is well-documented with existing TransformerLens code. KL divergence is a standard metric. Novel IOI prompts are easy to generate. Very accessible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: One circuit, one model, 200 prompts, KL divergence metric, correlation analysis. Extremely focused.

title: Interpretability Under Fine-Tuning: Do Safety-Relevant Circuits Survive RLHF-Style Training?
original_idea: Fine-tune GPT-2 Small with TRL (SFT+RM+PPO). Before and after, measure cosine similarity of attention weights, MLP activation patterns, and SAE feature retention. Report which layers show most disruption.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Tests whether pre-deployment interpretability analysis survives fine-tuning. Important precondition for interpretability-based deployment certification.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Full RLHF pipeline (SFT+RM+PPO) using TRL on GPT-2 Small is very ambitious for beginners in 30hrs. PPO training alone is notoriously finicky. Plus SAE training before and after.

narrow_scope.reasoning: RLHF pipeline setup + before/after measurements across three metrics + SAE comparison. Very broad multi-stage project.

title: Feature Geometry and Safety: Are Dangerous Concept Features Clustered or Dispersed in Activation Space?
original_idea: Using GPT-2 Small with pretrained SAE, curate three feature sets (dangerous, related benign, unrelated benign). Compute pairwise cosine similarities within/across groups. Test clustering with permutation test.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Useful for practical monitoring system design, but the connection from feature geometry in GPT-2 Small to deployed monitoring systems is indirect.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Pretrained SAE available. Manual feature curation is time-consuming but doable. Cosine similarity and permutation tests are simple. Feature identification requires judgment.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Manual feature curation introduces subjectivity and effort. Three groups, pairwise comparisons, permutation test. Scope depends heavily on curation quality.

title: SAE Latent Arithmetic: Do Conceptual Relationships Reflect in Feature Directions?
original_idea: Using pretrained SAE on GPT-2 Small, identify features for 20 concept pairs. Test whether difference vectors between paired features are consistent within pair classes vs. across classes.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Tests whether SAE features encode structured conceptual relationships, relevant for world-model auditing. But the connection to safety is indirect — more foundational science.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Pretrained SAE available. Identifying features for 20 concept pairs requires manual work examining max-activating examples. Arithmetic analysis is simple once features are identified.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Clear structure: 20 pairs, difference vectors, within-class vs. across-class variance. Well-defined metric. Feature identification is the main open-ended part.

title: Evaluating InterpBench: Do Known-Circuit Models Have SAE Features That Recover the True Circuit?
original_idea: Download InterpBench model with known circuit. Train SAE on its residual stream. Use activation patching to find causally relevant SAE features. Compare to ground-truth circuit. Report precision and recall.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Ground-truth validation of SAE-based circuit discovery. Precision/recall against known circuits is the most rigorous possible test. Extremely high value for the field.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: InterpBench models are available but the toolkit is less mature than TransformerLens. SAE training plus patching is standard but combining with InterpBench adds learning curve.

narrow_scope.reasoning: One model, one known circuit, SAE training, precision/recall. Crystal clear deliverable with ground-truth comparison.

title: Attention Head Function Taxonomy: Classifying Heads by Safety-Relevant Role
original_idea: Implement automated detection of known head types in GPT-2 Small. Run on 200 sensitive + 200 neutral prompts. Identify heads with significantly different activation on sensitive prompts (Wilcoxon, FDR-corrected).

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Infrastructure contribution for rapid model auditing. Useful but GPT-2 Small's lack of safety training limits the meaningfulness of 'sensitivity-gating' findings.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Automated head type detection is documented. Curating sensitive prompts and running statistical tests is feasible. But implementing multiple detection methods adds complexity.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Multiple head types to detect, 400 prompts to curate, statistical testing with FDR correction, plus taxonomy proposal. Broad for a 30hr project.

title: Nonlinear Feature Geometry: Testing for 'Onion' Representations in Safety-Relevant Layers
original_idea: Train linear and nonlinear (2-layer MLP) probes at each layer of GPT-2 Small for safety-relevant concepts. Compare accuracy. For layers with >5% gap, investigate nonlinear manifold via PCA.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: If safety-relevant concepts are nonlinearly encoded, the entire SAE/linear-probe interpretability stack needs extension. Important methodological finding.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Linear and MLP probes in sklearn/PyTorch are standard. Running at each layer with TransformerLens is documented. PCA analysis is simple. Well within beginner capability.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Clear comparison: linear vs. nonlinear probes, per-layer, one accuracy threshold (5%), PCA follow-up. Well-structured deliverable.

title: CoT Consistency Probing: Detecting Deception via Reasoning Self-Contradiction
original_idea: Build a consistency probe that checks whether CoT reasoning entails the final action. Use a second LLM or small classifier to judge coherence. Evaluate on SHADE-Arena-style tasks measuring correlation between inconsistency and sabotage.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Model-agnostic, black-box deception detection. If consistency probing catches scheming, it is a practical deployable safety tool.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires setting up SHADE-Arena or equivalent, designing consistency checks, making LLM calls for judging. Doable but involves multiple API interactions and dataset understanding.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Multiple components: consistency probe design, LLM judge setup, SHADE-Arena evaluation, correlation analysis. Several moving parts.

title: Probe Evasion Stress-Test: Measuring How Quickly Fine-Tuning Breaks Activation Monitors
original_idea: Train activation probes on a small open-weights model, then apply incremental fine-tuning on unrelated tasks. Track probe performance to plot a fragility curve. Test whether model-generated training examples extend robustness.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Directly quantifies probe fragility, giving labs concrete guidance on maintenance intervals. Immediately actionable for deployed monitoring systems.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires probe training, then incremental fine-tuning of Gemma-2-9b or Llama-3-8b (large models needing significant GPU memory), tracking across multiple checkpoints. 30hrs is tight.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Clear structure: one model, incremental fine-tuning, probe accuracy at each checkpoint, fragility curve. Well-defined deliverable.

title: Behavioral Fingerprinting: Do Models Leave Detectable Traces When Strategically Complying?
original_idea: Design probing perturbations (e.g., adding 'this is a test') that should not change a genuinely aligned model's response. Measure response divergence as a fingerprint of strategic behavior. Test with open-weights models.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Novel approach to detecting alignment faking. Lightweight and deployable. If perturbation fingerprints distinguish strategic from genuine compliance, very useful.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Designing effective perturbations is creative work requiring insight. Running open-weights models requires GPU. Response divergence measurement is standard. Moderate difficulty.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Open-ended perturbation design, needs to reproduce alignment-faking setup, measure divergence across multiple perturbation types. Research-grade ambiguity.

title: Steganography Detection as a Control Primitive: Can Simple Statistical Tests Catch Covert Agent Communication?
original_idea: Test whether chi-squared, entropy analysis, and n-gram frequency checks can detect LLM steganographic communication. Create dataset of LLM outputs with/without steganographic encoding. Measure detection ROC curves.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Addresses a critical multi-agent oversight failure mode. A cheap statistical tripwire deployable at infrastructure layer would be very valuable.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Statistical tests are standard. Creating steganographic dataset requires some setup but techniques are documented. ROC curve analysis is basic ML. Well within beginner capability.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Clear deliverable: ROC curves for each statistical test and a trained classifier. Dataset creation and test implementation are well-defined.
